# Probability that Sum of 100 Exponentials ≤ 215

## Identifying the Parameters

Each random variable $\xi_i$ follows an exponential distribution with rate $\lambda = 0.5$:

$$f(x) = 0.5\,e^{-0.5x}, \quad x \geq 0$$

For an $\text{Exp}(\lambda)$ distribution:
$$\mathbb{E}[\xi_i] = \frac{1}{\lambda} = 2, \qquad \text{Var}(\xi_i) = \frac{1}{\lambda^2} = 4$$

## Statistics of the Sum

Let $S = \sum_{i=1}^{100} \xi_i$. Since the variables are independent:

$$\mathbb{E}[S] = 100 \times 2 = 200$$

$$\text{Var}(S) = 100 \times 4 = 400 \implies \sigma_S = 20$$

## Applying the Central Limit Theorem

By the CLT, for $n = 100$ (sufficiently large), the standardized sum is approximately standard normal:

$$Z = \frac{S - \mathbb{E}[S]}{\sigma_S} = \frac{S - 200}{20} \;\approx\; N(0,1)$$

## Computing the Probability

$$P(S \leq 215) \;=\; P\!\left(\frac{S - 200}{20} \leq \frac{215 - 200}{20}\right) \;=\; P(Z \leq 0.75)$$

Looking up the standard normal CDF:

$$\Phi(0.75) = 0.7734$$

## Result

$$\boxed{0.7734}$$
